results.title: Banks court religious communities with tailored financial services
results.content: Korea's major banks are courting religious communities to expand their customer base, offering tailored services such as mobile donation platforms and debit cards that double as membership cards for religious groups, industry officials said Monday. Hana Bank's mobile donation service for religious organizations processed 68 billion won ($51 million) in donations from January through October this year, according to the bank. This is a sharp increase from the 350 million won recorded in 2020, when the service was first introduced. The service allows worshippers at churches and Buddhist temples to make donations using QR codes, without having to install a separate app. Religious organizations can also link transaction data to their financial management systems, making it easier to issue donation receipts for year-end tax deductions. results.title: Ex-deputy national security adviser takes office as KOICA chief
results.content: Oh Hyun-joo, a career diplomat who previously served as a deputy director at the presidential National Security Office, took office Monday as the 15th president of the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), the state-run foreign aid agency. KOICA is Korea’s main agency for carrying out the government’s grant aid programs for developing countries. It was founded in 1991. An inauguration ceremony was held the same day at its headquarters in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. Oh graduated from Korea University with a degree in Spanish language and literature and earned a master’s degree in international relations from the University of Cambridge. She joined the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in 1994 after passing the foreign service exam. results.title: Local Oxford imprint aims to bring more Korean stories to English readers
results.content: Korean literature is set to reach more English-speaking readers through a new publishing imprint established by Oxford University's Korean studies center. The Oxford Centre for Korean Studies (OCKS) said Monday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with a local independent publisher, Oxford eBooks, to establish K-PRESS — a new imprint dedicated to translating Korean literature into English, according to Yonhap News Agency. The first title to be published will be “Mother Star,” the English edition of actor and novelist Cha In-pyo's debut novel. Jieun Kiaer, director of the center, told Yonhap that barriers to translation and publication remain high, with English-language editions concentrated among a small number of Korean writers and genres. She expressed hope that K-PRESS would introduce a wider range of stories reflecting Korean lives, emotions, humor and imagination. K-PRESS als

results.title: As DUI scandals rock Korean entertainment, Super Junior star's unusual decision resurfaces
results.content: As drunk driving scandals have repeatedly derailed celebrity careers in Korea and often forcing stars to suspend their activities or withdraw from the public eye, Super Junior member Kim Hee-chul's unusual decision to sell his car to eliminate the temptation to drive after drinking is drawing renewed attention following a recent incident involving actor Ko Kyung-pyo. Ko, known for his role in the hit Korean drama "Reply 1988," posted a lengthy apology on social media Sunday after crashing into a street-cleaning truck while driving under the influence (DUI) early Saturday. The collision left the truck's driver, a man in his 60s, injured. Ko's blood alcohol concentration reportedly exceeded Korea's legal threshold for driver's license revocation. results.title: HD Hyundai Heavy wins $203.6 mil. order for 4 LPG carriers
results.content: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries said Monday it has secured a 272.1 billion-won ($203.6 million) contract to build four liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carriers. The South Korean shipbuilder said it will build the vessels for an undisclosed client in Oceania and deliver them by September 2029. The latest contract accounts for 1.55 percent of the company's annual sales, according to its regulatory filing.

results.title: Lee's Kosdaq reform push faces skepticism over lack of concrete measures
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung’s push to revive Kosdaq as part of broader capital market reforms is drawing skepticism, with market participants saying Monday that his proposals lack concrete measures to attract investment. They support removing weak companies and broadening the investor base but question whether the measures outlined so far will bring sustained capital inflows. At a policy meeting at the Korea Exchange on Friday, Lee acknowledged widespread concerns about Kosdaq and called for stricter enforcement of delisting rules to swiftly remove financially troubled or underperforming companies. The meeting followed steep declines in both KOSPI and Kosdaq from record highs earlier this year, fueling concerns about financial market stability. results.title: Seoul to transform hidden Sinchon hilltop into sunset, night-view park by 2027
results.content: A hidden hilltop park tucked just an eight-minute walk from Seoul’s bustling Sinchon university district is set to undergo a major transformation into a premier night tourism landmark by 2027. Seodaemun District said Monday that Changcheon Neighborhood Park, commonly known by locals as Baramsan (Wind Mountain) due to its breezy elevated terrain, has been selected for the Seoul Metropolitan Government's 2026 Seoul Starlight Attraction Creation Project. The district plans to invest up to 1 billion won in municipal funding following final budget reviews, supported by 50 million won in district funds already secured for initial master planning. The project aims to leverage Baramsan's sweeping urban views to create a dedicated sunset and night-view destination, linking the hilltop park directly to the vibrant commercial and dining strip along Yonsei-ro to stimulate nighttime tourism and local

results.title: Culture ministry to host forum on AI use in culture, sports, tourism
results.content: The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism will host a forum Tuesday on how artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in culture, sports and tourism and on how these sectors should shift to AI. The ministry said Monday the fourth Culture, Sports and Tourism Digital Innovation Forum, themed “New Culture Through AI,” will be held at L Tower in Seoul’s Seocho District. About 400 people from government, public institutions and the private sector are expected to attend. State-affiliated bodies are co-organizing the event, including the Korea Culture Information Service Agency, Arts Council Korea, the Korea Sports Promotion Foundation, the Korea Tourism Organization and the Korea Creative Content Agency. results.title: Pulmuone Food & Culture opens first overseas catering operation in US
results.content: Pulmuone Food & Culture opened its first overseas contract catering operation in the United States, bringing Korean food to a workplace in Arizona as the company looks to expand its food service business across North America. The food service subsidiary of Pulmuone said Monday that it began operating a cafeteria at a Korean conglomerate's facility in Queen Creek, Arizona, marking its first overseas contract catering operation. The operation is run through Pulmuone FNC USA, the company's U.S. subsidiary established in January, and occupies 175 pyeong, or about 578 square meters, including dining and kitchen areas. The cafeteria currently serves lunch and dinner, with menus designed for both Korean employees and local staff. Its offerings follow a dual-track approach, combining traditional Korean dishes with familiar American meals. Korean options include galbijjim, or braised short ribs,

results.title: Namdaemun merchants part of Seoul traditional markets' Naver Live shopping push
results.content: Namdaemun Market accessories and local food specialties are heading to smartphone screens as Seoul's Jung District is set to host a live commerce broadcast on Naver Shopping Live on Wednesday, connecting small business merchants with nationwide online shoppers. The district office announced that six merchants across five local commercial hubs — including Namdaemun Market, Jungbu Market, Shin Jungbu Market, Shin Jungang Market and Donghwa-dong Alley Shopping District — will participate in the day-long event. Four merchants will offer food items, including artisanal sesame and perilla oils from Donghwa-dong, dried seaweed from Jungbu Market, nuts and dried seafood from Shin Jungbu Market and traditional sweet puffed wheat snacks from Shin Jungang Market. results.title: OCI Holdings and OCI earn A grades in 2026 ESG assessment
results.content: Chemical and renewable energy materials giant OCI Holdings and its basic chemicals unit OCI have both earned overall A grades in Korea's latest corporate sustainability assessment, lifted by improvements in governance, environmental management and workplace safety. The companies said Monday they received the ratings in the 2026 assessment conducted by the Korea Institute of Corporate Governance and Sustainability, which evaluates listed companies across environmental, social and governance categories using a seven-tier grading system. OCI Holdings improved its overall rating to A from B+ last year, driven largely by stronger governance practices. Its governance grade also rose to A from B+, reflecting efforts to strengthen board independence, internal auditing and corporate oversight. The company increased the proportion of independent directors on board committees from 80 percent to 100

results.title: Students unveil AI tools to solve social challenges
results.content: Ten teams of undergraduate and graduate students showcased six months of social innovation projects in Seoul last week, presenting solutions ranging from artificial intelligence tools that ease special education teachers' workloads to an app helping visually impaired pedestrians cross streets safely. Hosted by the Seoul Future Talent Foundation at its community center, the 2026 Seoul Impact Project showcase highlighted student-led initiatives tackling persistent social challenges. After evaluating presentations, a judging panel awarded 15 million won ($10,800) in combined prize money to three standout teams. Aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, the program supports teams of two to five students creating public value. Selected through a three-stage screening process, each of the 10 teams received 5 million won in project funding and 2 million won per member in ac

results.title: SK Telecom, Hyosung team up to build AI data center power infrastructure
results.content: SK Telecom signed a strategic partnership agreement with Hyosung Heavy Industries to secure power equipment and explore new technologies for gigawatt-scale artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, the telecom company said Monday. The memorandum of understanding covers equipment supplies for 345-kilovolt substations, joint testing of next-generation power technologies and potential cooperation in developing and building new AI data centers. SK Telecom CEO Jung Jai-hun and Hyosung Heavy Industries CEO Woo Tae-hee signed the agreement at SK Telecom's headquarters in central Seoul. Their discussions also covered various business cooperation opportunities involving AI power infrastructure. The partnership combines SK Telecom's experience in developing and operating AI data centers with Hyosung Heavy Industries' power equipment manufacturing and engineering capabilities. results.title: PM pledges to bring home remains of every single independence fighter from overseas
results.content: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook renewed the government's commitment Monday to bringing the remains of independence fighters back home from overseas as she marked the return of the remains of two patriots who fought for Korea's independence from Japan's 1910-45 colonial rule. The remains of Ho Si-han and Lee Gwal arrived Sunday from the United States and Uzbekistan, respectively, and the government held an official ceremony at Seodaemun Independence Park in central Seoul on Monday to commemorate their return. The remains will be buried at the national cemetery in the central city of Daejeon. "I offer my infinite respect to the two patriots who, with indomitable courage and spirit, forged ahead through a treacherous, thorn-strewn path for the sake of our nation's independence," Han said. "The government will uphold the noble spirit of patriotic martyrs, with a firm commitment never to forget

results.title: JTBC terminates Olympic broadcast deal amid financial woes
results.content: Debt-ridden broadcaster JTBC said Monday it has terminated its contract with the International Olympic Committee to air the Olympics in Korea. "With the contract termination, JTBC has eliminated financial uncertainties and established a more stable foundation for management," the company said, adding the decision was made as it was difficult to maintain its Olympic broadcast business. The financial details of the decision will be included in the company's third-quarter regulatory filing, the company said. JTBC had secured the broadcast rights for the Winter and Summer Olympics from 2026-2032 and for the World Cup from 2026-2030. In August, a Seoul court approved the broadcaster's request to begin rehabilitation proceedings, allowing the company to restructure its debts under court supervision. results.title: Honoring a bygone Korean industrialist
results.content: A posthumous award presented to a renowned Korean industrialist who passed away two years ago was a notable highlight of a recent ceremony. The honor was bestowed at the Grand Walkerhill Seoul on Nov. 6. The event, attended by approximately 300 military personnel and civilians, including the newly appointed U.S. Ambassador to Korea Michelle Park Steel and her husband, was held as part of the 24th Korea-America Friendship Night, an annual gathering organized by the Korea-America Association (KAA), headed by Choi Joong-kyung. Following careful deliberation, the KAA's citation committee selected Cho Suck-rai (1935–2024), former honorary chairman of Hyosung Group, as this year's recipient. Cho studied applied chemistry at Waseda University in Japan before earning a master's degree in chemical engineering from the Illinois Institute of Technology in the United States. results.title: Major crimes unit's Seoul office raids restaurant franchisor in 1st search operation
results.content: The Seoul Regional Office of the Serious Crime Investigation Agency (SCIA) raided the restaurant franchisor Myeong Ryun Dang Co. on Monday over allegations of unfair affiliate support, marking its first search and seizure operation since its establishment last month. SCIA investigators began searching 26 locations, including the company's headquarters in Seoul's southern district of Songpa and the residence of company Chairman Lee Jong-geun, at around 9 a.m. Myeong Ryun Dang, the operator of the Myeongryun Jinsa Galbi barbecue restaurant franchise with stores at home and abroad, is accused of providing unfair financial support to 14 lending companies owned by Lee by extending loans totaling 298.3 billion won (US$223 million) at annual interest rates of between 2.3 percent and 4.6 percent over a period of more than four years starting in late 2021. results.title: Seoul to closely monitor N. Korean official's Russia trip before Trump-Xi-Putin summit
results.content: The unification ministry said Monday it is closely watching a senior North Korean official's trip to Moscow, which comes just days before a planned summit of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia. Jo Yong-won, a secretary of the Central Committee of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea (WPK), has been visiting Moscow since Saturday as the head of a party and government delegation, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). He is known as a close aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. The KCNA said the visit comes as the "militant friendship" and "relations of alliance" between Pyongyang and Moscow grow stronger "with each passing day." The purpose and schedule of the trip have not been disclosed. results.title: N. Korea praises women as 'real revolutionaries' on Mother's Day
results.content: North Korea on Monday celebrated the country's Mothers' Day, praising women as "real revolutionaries" and "patriots," and noting that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has elevated their status to the "highest level." In an article honoring mothers, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) stressed the crucial role of mothers in the country, saying they are getting respect and love in a social atmosphere that honors mothers devoted to their families and society. It also pointed out leader Kim's efforts to recognize mothers' dedication to society, including creating Mothers' Day and instituting an honorary award for mothers who have contributed to enhancing the country's prosperity. results.title: FTC initiates consent resolution process for chauffeur service providers
results.content: Korea's antitrust watchdog said Monday it has initiated a consent resolution process involving two designated driver service providers and two driver dispatch software operators over alleged unfair practices, including effectively imposing sales targets through a driver rating system. The Fair Trade Commission's (FTC) move concerns Kakao Mobility Corp. and T Map Mobility Co., affiliated with Kakao Corp. and SK Group, respectively, as well as driver dispatch software operators CMNP and YLP, over suspected violations of the Fair Trade Act. Kakao Mobility sold its entire stake in CMNP late last year but maintains a business partnership with the company, while YLP is wholly owned by T Map Mobility. results.title: Seoul rolls out comprehensive transit measures for college entrance exam takers
results.content: Seoul will add subway runs, adjust bus schedules and offer free emergency rides to help students reach their test sites on time for Thursday’s College Scholastic Ability Test, the city government said. The annual exam is the main standardized test used for university admissions in Korea. This year, 113,454 students will take the exam at 228 sites in Seoul. They must enter their test sites between 6:30 a.m. and 8:10 a.m. To ease morning traffic, the workday at the city government, district offices and other public institutions will start one hour later than usual, at 10 a.m. Subways will make 27 extra runs between 6 a.m. and 10 a.m., and 15 trains will be kept on standby in case of breakdowns. results.title: Seoul battery tests reveal heightened fire risks at full charge
results.content: Lithium-ion batteries charged to full capacity were far more likely to catch fire or undergo thermal runaway when subjected to external pressure, according to tests released by Seoul on Monday, raising questions about safety practices in warehouses storing large quantities of batteries. The Seoul Metropolitan Fire and Disaster Headquarters said four out of five batteries in both cylindrical and pouch-shaped categories experienced thermal runaway and ignition when charged to 100 percent. The tests were conducted by the headquarters’ Fire Investigation Research Center following a July fire at a logistics center in Incheon, as authorities examined whether battery charge levels should be regulated during distribution and storage. results.title: Deoksu Palace's Seokjojeon Hall to host free Mozart, Brahms concert
results.content: A string quintet will play Mozart and Brahms at Seokjojeon Hall in Deoksu Palace, central Seoul, on Nov. 25. The concert is free and takes place inside a landmark of Korea’s last imperial court. The Deoksu Palace Management Office under the Korea Heritage Service said Monday it will co-host the 7 p.m. concert with the Kumho Cultural Foundation. The theme is “Bulmang Chosim,” a Korean expression meaning “never forget the heart you started with.” Seokjojeon was completed in 1910. It was the first Western-style stone building commissioned by Emperor Gojong (1852-1919) of the Korean Empire (1897-1910), the short-lived monarchy that preceded Japanese colonial rule. Records show a Korean pianist performed there after it was finished. Based on that history, the two organizations have run the concert series since 2018. results.title: Seoul opens royal palace, museums for twilight weddings
results.content: Couples looking to avoid the assembly-line rush of commercial wedding halls can now exchange vows under the evening sky at some of Seoul’s most storied landmarks. The Seoul Metropolitan Government hosted its inaugural Romantic Night Wedding on Saturday evening at Unhyeon Palace, a historic royal residence in central Seoul, marking the launch of a city initiative that opens cultural heritage sites and public museums for after-hours nuptials. Under soft courtyard lighting, a 35-year-old couple dressed in traditional Korean wedding attire held a ceremony at Norakdang Hall, the very pavilion where King Gojong and Empress Myeongseong celebrated their royal wedding during the Joseon Dynasty (1392–1897). results.title: 'Rohtko' dazzles in Seoul, but leaves its cultural hierarchies unresolved
results.content: What makes a work of art authentic and who determines its value? Does a fake piece of art change how people feel about it? “Rohtko,” a play inspired by a multimillion-dollar art forgery scandal that rattled the art world in 2009, brought those increasingly resonant questions to its Korean premiere, drawing enthusiastic theatergoers. Polish director Lukasz Twarkowski’s multimedia production arrived at LG Arts Center in Seoul for its Nov. 13-15 Korean premiere, four years after its European debut. Winner of five Latvian theater awards and Italy’s Ubu Award for best foreign production, it brought considerable European acclaim to an eagerly anticipated Seoul audience. The sheer scale of the production’s inventive mise-en-scene clearly impressed many Korean theatergoers. Its visual spectacle was undeniable. results.title: Murder of runaway teen exposes gaps in protection system
results.content: The murder of a 15-year-old girl in Seoul's Seongbuk District has drawn attention to the dangers posed by adults who approach runaway teenagers with promises of food and shelter but may exploit them for criminal purposes. The case has also raised concerns about gaps in Korea's protection system for young people living away from home amid allegations that the victim, who had been moving between youth shelters, was coerced into prostitution and other criminal activities. According to police and other authorities Sunday, a 59-year-old man surnamed Jin, who was arrested on suspicion of killing the girl at a shared accommodation facility in Jeongneung-dong, Seongbuk District, was formally detained Friday and remains under police investigation. results.title: Korean heritage souvenirs fuel 41% sales surge at Seoul design landmark
results.content: Seoul-themed souvenirs are finding buyers well beyond traditional gift shops, with products reimagining Korean heritage for everyday use helping drive a 41.2 percent surge in sales this year at the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), a futuristic architectural landmark and design hub in the capital. The store, operated by the Seoul Design Foundation, recorded 2.734 billion won ($2.05 million) in revenue and 654,797 visitors from January through October, up 41.2 percent and 4.7 percent, respectively, from the same period last year, the foundation said Monday. The store featured 2,806 products from 194 design brands, including Seoul-themed stickers, baseball caps, character merchandise and decorative accessories combining local identity with practical design. results.title: Huawei marks 11 years of efforts to nurture ICT talent in Korea
results.content: Huawei said Monday it has sponsored the 2026 International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) Seoul Regional, extending its efforts to nurture information and communications technology talent in Korea to 11 straight years. The contest, held from Friday to Saturday, at KINTEX exhibition hall in Goyang, Gyeonggi Province, was participated by around 80 teams from Korea, Japan, Singapore and other Asian universities. It is a regional edition of the ICPC, one of the world’s largest university programming competitions attracting some 50,000 participants from more than 100 countries annually. results.title: Starfield Library decorates Christmas with goblin Santa, palace-inspired tree
results.content: Starfield Library, the famous library inside Coex Mall in southern Seoul, kicked off a Korean-themed holiday campaign. Its centerpiece is a character inspired by a dokkaebi, a mythical Korean goblin, who transforms into Santa Claus. Mall operator Shinsegae Property said its “Read the Library” campaign runs through Jan. 31, 2027, under the theme “Dokkaebi Santa and Christmas.” A dokkaebi is a mischievous goblin from Korean folklore. At the center of the campaign is “Five More Minutes of Christmas,” a short fantasy story written for it by Lee Miye, author of the bestselling novel “The Dallergut Dream Department Store.” In the story, a goblin hears a child wish that Christmas could last five more minutes. results.title: HD Hyundai targets North American energy market with solar, battery technologies
results.content: HD Hyundai, a Korean shipbuilding, heavy machinery and energy conglomerate, will showcase its latest solar power, energy storage and power grid technologies at North America’s largest clean energy exhibition this week, as the industrial group seeks to expand its presence in the rapidly growing U.S. energy market. HD Hyundai Energy Solutions and HD Hyundai Electric will jointly participate in RE+ 2026, which runs from Tuesday through Thursday at Las Vegas Convention Center, company officials said Monday. The two affiliates will present technologies spanning solar power generation, energy storage and conversion, and electricity transmission and distribution, highlighting their integrated capabilities across energy infrastructure.
